plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single sketch on an unlabeled coordinate plane showing a position vector broken into its horizontal and vertical parts. Two thin axes with arrowheads at all four ends meet at the origin; neither axis carries a name or numbers, though a few short tick marks are spaced along them. An orange arrow runs from the origin up and to the right into the first quadrant and is labeled v = ai + bj, with v, i, and j set in bold. A dark blue arrow extends from the origin along the horizontal axis to the point lying directly beneath the orange arrow's tip and is labeled ai below the axis. A second dark blue arrow rises vertically from that point to the tip of the orange arrow and is labeled bj. The two blue arrows and the orange one enclose a right triangle whose legs are the components and whose hypotenuse is the vector. Drawing the components as arrows joined head to tail makes the vector read as their sum rather than as an abstract pair. The sketch supports the magnitude of v being sqrt(a^2 + b^2), read straight off the legs of the triangle.

interactionPlan.concept: A position vector v = ai + bj is the head-to-tail sum of its horizontal and vertical component vectors, and those components form the legs of a right triangle whose hypotenuse length is |v| = sqrt(a² + b²).
elements: Thin black horizontal axis with arrowheads at both ends, a few short unlabeled tick marks
Thin black vertical axis with arrowheads at both ends, a few short unlabeled tick marks
Origin point where the axes cross
Orange arrow from origin into the first quadrant representing the vector v
Bold italic label 'v = ai + bj' placed in the upper-left region near the orange arrow
Dark blue horizontal arrow from origin along the x-axis to (a, 0), the component ai
Label 'ai' (bold i) below the horizontal blue arrow
Dark blue vertical arrow from (a, 0) up to (a, b), the component bj
Label 'bj' (bold j) to the right of the vertical blue arrow
Right-angle square marker at (a, 0) between the two blue arrows (shown in triangle view)
Dashed light-gray guide lines from the vector tip to each axis (magnitude view)
Numeric side-length labels 'a', 'b' and hypotenuse label '√(a² + b²)' shown in the magnitude view
Readout panel showing current a, b, and computed |v|
Legend keying orange = resultant vector v, dark blue = component vectors

interactions.label: a (horizontal component)
interactions.teaches: The ai arrow stretches or flips along the x-axis and drags the tip of v sideways, isolating the purely horizontal share of the vector.

interactions.label: b (vertical component)
interactions.teaches: The bj arrow grows or shrinks vertically from the end of ai, moving the tip of v up or down and isolating the purely vertical share.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The same picture read two ways: as a head-to-tail sum of component vectors, or as a right triangle whose legs |a| and |b| give |v| = sqrt(a² + b²).

demo_steps.title: The vector and its parts
demo_steps.narration: An orange arrow v reaches into the first quadrant. Two dark blue arrows, ai along the x-axis and bj rising from its tip, are joined head to tail and land exactly on v's tip.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the horizontal part
demo_steps.narration: Increasing a lengthens only the ai arrow; the tip of v slides right and the vector tilts flatter, while bj is untouched.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the vertical part
demo_steps.narration: Now raise b. Only bj grows, the tip climbs, and v steepens — the two components act completely independently.

demo_steps.title: A negative component flips direction
demo_steps.narration: Set a negative and the ai arrow points left, carrying v into the second quadrant. The sum rule still holds: v always ends where bj ends.

demo_steps.title: Read off the magnitude
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the triangle view: the components become labeled legs with a right angle between them, and the hypotenuse is |v| = sqrt(a² + b²).

demo_steps.title: Watch the hypotenuse respond
demo_steps.narration: Change either leg and the hypotenuse updates by the Pythagorean theorem — length depends on both components, but never on their signs.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: ai and bj are not just labels on a pair of numbers — they are actual arrows laid head to tail, so the vector IS their sum and its length is automatically the hypotenuse of the right triangle they form.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Center the origin in the plotting area with a plain unlabeled cross of thin black axes, arrowheads at all four ends, and a handful of small evenly spaced tick marks on each. Draw the resultant v as a medium-weight orange arrow from the origin to (a, b); draw ai as a dark navy arrow from the origin along the x-axis to (a, 0) and bj as a dark navy arrow from (a, 0) to (a, b), each with a solid arrowhead. Label 'v = ai + bj' in bold serif math near the interior upper-left of the vector, 'ai' just below the horizontal arrow, 'bj' just right of the vertical arrow. In the magnitude-triangle view, keep the same geometry but lighten the component arrows to plain line segments, add a small right-angle square at (a, 0), replace the arrow labels with numeric leg lengths, and annotate the orange hypotenuse with '|v| = √(a² + b²)' plus its computed value. Keep the drawing region symmetric so negative a or b still fits on screen; a small readout in a corner shows the live a, b, and |v|.
interactionPlan.figureCaption: CNX_Precalc_Figure_08_08_010 — a position vector resolved into horizontal and vertical component vectors.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for a: the learner changes the horizontal component, the ai arrow length and the endpoint of v move left or right, and the horizontal part of ai + bj is separated from the vertical part.
- Slider for b: the learner changes the vertical component, the bj arrow height and the endpoint of v move up or down, and the vertical part of the vector sum becomes visible.
- Toggle between components and magnitude triangle: the learner switches from labeled component arrows to a right-triangle view with side lengths and sqrt(a^2 + b^2), showing why the vector magnitude follows the Pythagorean theorem.

Plot showing vectors in rectangular coordinates in terms of i and j. The position vector v (in orange) extends from the origin to some point (a,b) in Q1. The horizontal (ai) and vertical (bj) components are shown.

discrepancies: In the source, the v = ai + bj label sits clearly to the left of the orange arrow in open space; in the generated figure it is placed so close to the orange vector that the text overlaps/touches the arrow shaft, hurting legibility.

The source shows only a few sparse tick marks (one or two per axis) with no origin dot; the generated figure adds many evenly spaced ticks on all four axis directions plus a filled dot at the origin, giving a busier coordinate-grid look than the original.
Extra on-canvas chrome not in the source: a bottom-left legend ('resultant v' / 'components a i , b j') and a top-right numeric readout 'a = 4 b = 3 |v| = 5.00'.

Axis proportions differ: the source axes are cropped tightly around the vector (short axis stubs), while the generated axes span a much larger plot with the vector occupying a small central region, making the vector appear smaller relative to the frame.

The source's axis arrowheads and vector arrowheads are similar in weight; in the generated figure the y-axis extends far above/below with long stems, changing the compositional balance of the original.
evaluation.notes: Structurally faithful reproduction of the orange resultant with head-to-tail navy components and correct italic/bold vector notation, backed by genuinely useful sliders, a triangle-view toggle and a 6-step guided demo; main weaknesses are the v = ai + bj label colliding with the orange arrow, extra legend/readout chrome absent from the source, and a denser tick pattern with an oversized axis frame that shrinks the vector.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interaction structure are correct; remaining issues are execution details—label collision with the arrow, extra legend/readout chrome, excess ticks, and axis scaling—which are generator-level fixes.
